narrative.overview:
Confident Demo pairs a direct Expert Advisor offer with a working-looking, code-native product surface: workflow nodes, sample data, clear demo limits, and a visible license decision. It is product-led rather than promotional, and it makes the evaluation path easy to understand before purchase.

The system is sober, technical, and transparent. Charcoal surfaces, warm ivory type, cool slate rules, champagne transaction signals, condensed type, and square construction create a world that feels issued and verifiable without pretending to be a live broker dashboard. It rejects trading-dashboard spectacle, editorial newsprint, decorative finance imagery, and any visual implication of guaranteed performance.
keyCharacteristics: The license term is treated as a primary product attribute, not a badge or pricing footnote.
Fine registration lines and divided fields organize content instead of floating card stacks.
Champagne is rare and transactional: selection, price, focus, and the next action.
Public product facts and private intellectual property are separated visibly and plainly.
Dense technical labels coexist with readable, direct body copy and explicit risk language.

rules.name: The Champagne Transaction Rule
rules.body: Champagne identifies a decision, amount, state, or next action; it is never a general background decoration.

rules.name: The Mineral Field Rule
rules.body: Use tonal surfaces and fine rules to create hierarchy; do not introduce arbitrary card colors.

rules.name: The Condensed Signal Rule
rules.body: Use Barlow Condensed for structure, numbers, and issued labels; use Barlow for sentences and guidance.

rules.name: The Contiguous Field Rule
rules.body: Prefer one framed field subdivided by rules over a collection of detached cards with independent spacing.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: A shadow must communicate an overlay; it must never be used to make a static section feel more premium.

rules.name: The Issued Edge Rule
rules.body: Keep core controls at 0–1px corner radius and reserve the small utility curve for secondary interface mechanics.

rules.name: The One Decision Signal Rule
rules.body: Within a commercial module, one champagne action owns the decision while every other control remains structural or textual.

dos: Do make duration, price, scope, and next action readable as one licensing decision.
Do preserve the charcoal, graphite, cool-slate, and champagne hierarchy across routes.
Do use linework, aligned fields, and condensed labels to make technical information scannable.
Do keep public product facts separate from protected source code, strategy logic, parameters, and optimization material.
Do state risk and unconnected payment or activation states plainly wherever they affect a decision.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, readable contrast, reduced motion, and a 320px minimum responsive target.
donts: Don't use trading dashboards, price charts, crypto motifs, or imagery that implies live performance.
Don't use editorial newsprint, serif display type, beige paper, or a magazine-like composition.
Don't use gradients, glow, glass effects, soft card stacks, or pill-shaped commercial controls.
Don't turn champagne into a decorative wash or allow multiple primary actions to compete.
Don't publish private implementation details or invent performance, compatibility, certification, activation, or payment claims.
